nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ag NWs
nodes.procedure: An oil bath method was used to synthesize Ag NWs according to our previous report57. Specifically, a mix solution consisting of ethylene glycol, FeCl3 (7.19 mM), AgNO3 (0.051 M), and polyvinylpyrrolidone (0.012 M) was heat and maintained under an oil bath pan with 110°C for 12 h. After that, the generated precipitate was washed with acetone and alcohol to get the pure Ag NWs.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiO/Ni on Ag NWs
nodes.procedure: Ni/NiO is grown on Ag NWs network by a facile electrodeposition process in the aqueous electrolyte of 20 mM C4H6NiO4·4H2O according to the recent report36. The electrodeposition process was performed by chronoamperometry method with -3 V versus SCE for 200 s under a standard three-electrode system, in which graphite sheet acted as a counter electrode, SCE acted as a reference electrode, and the fabricated Ag NWs network loaded on the cloth was directly used as working electrode. The obtained samples were washed with deionized water and then dried at room temperature.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of metallic Ni on Ag NWs
nodes.procedure: Metallic Ni is grown on Ag NWs network by the electrodeposition process in an aqueous solution consisting of 0.10-M NiCl2, 0.09-M H3BO3 and a solvent containing ethanol and deionized water with 2:5 in volume ratio. The electrodeposition process was performed by chronoamperometry with -1.2 V versus SCE for 200 s. The obtained samples were washed with deionized water and then dried at room temperature.

nodes.name: Electroreduction of Pt single atoms on NiO/Ni
nodes.procedure: PtSA-NiO/Ni on Ag NWs was fabricated by the electrochemical reduction process in the three-electrode system, in which the fabricated NiO/Ni on Ag NWs was performed as the working electrode, graphite sheet acted as a counter electrode, saturated calomel electrode acted as a reference electrode. The corresponding electrochemical process was carried out by multi-cycle cathode polarization in 1-M KOH solution containing 50-μM H2PtCl6 with a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ between 0 and -0.50 V versus RHE for 200 cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Pt characteristic peaks detected in PtSA-NiO/Ni, implying absence of Pt clusters and particles; only metallic Ni signal without distinctive NiO peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phase evolution of samples is investigated by XRD pattern as shown in Fig. 2a, in which no Pt characteristic peaks are detected, implying the absence of Pt cluster and particles in PtSA-NiO/Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA-NiO/Ni shows well-distributed and open 3D nanosheets morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM (Fig. 2b, c) images show the well-distributed and open 3D nanosheets morphology for PtSA-NiO/Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright spots along NiO/Ni interfaces confirm atomically dispersed Pt single atoms; magnified image shows Pt atoms mostly at NiO/Ni heterostructure interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular darkfield STEM (HAADF-STEM, Fig. 2d) image displays bright spots along with the interfaces of NiO/Ni heterostructure... The magnified HAADF-STEM image (Fig. 2e) suggests that the single Pt atoms are mostly immobilized at the interfaces of the NiO/Ni heterostructure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Distinct lattice fringes of 0.18 nm match metallic Ni (200) planes; FFT shows Ni (200) ring and diffused halo for NiO phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM shows one distinct lattice fringes of 0.18 nm, matching well with metallic Ni (200) crystallographic planes (Fig. 2h). The FFT pattern (inset in Fig. 2h) shows four distinct rings: the red ring corresponds to the metallic Ni (200) plane, and the yellow rings with the highly diffused halo are assigned to the NiO phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows Pt atoms uniformly dispersed throughout NiO/Ni nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the elemental mapping, SEM image, and HAADF-STEM image (Figs. 2i–n and S18–20) show that Pt atoms are uniformly dispersed throughout NiO/Ni nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f spectra show positive shift vs Pt foil indicating charge transfer from Pt to supports; PtSA-NiO shows largest shift; both metallic Pt and Pt(IV) species present.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f spectrums of PtSA-NiO/Ni, PtSA-NiO, and PtSA-Ni are close to Pt0 but show some positive shift with different extents compared with Pt foil... the fitting curve of Pt XPS spectrums display Pt(IV) species in the samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES white-line intensity decreases from PtSA-NiO (+1.23 valence) to PtSA-NiO/Ni (+0.73 valence) to PtSA-Ni (+0.29 valence), indicating increasing Pt 5d occupancy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3c, the average valence state of Pt increase from +0.29, +0.73, to +1.23 for the Pt-Ni, Pt-NiO/Ni, and PtSA-NiO catalysts, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Pt-Pt scattering at ~2.7 Å confirms atomic Pt dispersion across all catalysts. PtSA-NiO/Ni: CN Pt-O=1.3, Pt-Ni=5.8; PtSA-NiO: CN Pt-O=2.4, Pt-Ni=2.1; PtSA-Ni: CN Pt-Ni=4.9.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the typical Pt-Pt contribution peak of Pt foil at about 2.7 Å is absent... the first-shell EXAFS fitting of PtSA-NiO/Ni sample gives a coordination number (CN) of 1.3 for Pt–O contribution and 5.8 for Pt–Ni contribution.
